(B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
(Repeatx2) Observed no food handlers licenses to be available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, staff will all take the steps to receive license this week. Ensure any employee that handles food has completed the required food handlers training after 3 days of employment. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the sani bucket to be 100 ppm. Inspector asked the employee to re-make the sani bucket. 200 ppm of quaternary ammonium. Ensure sani buckets are frequently changed in order to maintain appropriate concentrations. Quat: 200-400 ppm. Utilize test strips to verify concentration. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below). 

Observed an open bottle of Comet sitting on a shelf above food contact utensils and bowls. Discussed with PIC and relocated. Ensure potentially poisonous materials are stored below or away food contact surfaces.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

Observed coffee stir sticks to be sitting in a soiled container. Discussed with PIC and cleaned. Ensure food contact utensil storage is cleaned at a frequency to prevent soiling.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

Observed multiple utensils and pots to be accumulating food debris on the shelving left of the triple sink. Discussed with PIC. Ensure equipment is stored and cleaned at a frequency to prevent contamination before use.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed multiple sample spoons to not have handle facing upward. Discussed with PIC and replaced. Ensure single service utensils are stored in a way to prevent contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Observed food debris behind the lid of the prep cooler. PIC is instructed to clean often enough so as to maintain the area clean.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

The walk in cooler fans have a thick accumulation of dust. The situation was discussed with the PIC.  Clean prior to the next routine inspection and maintain clean moving forward.

findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Multiple locations throughout the facility are in need of cleaning during this inspection. Areas include: 1) the ceiling tiles around the air intakes; 2) floors into corners and under shelves. PIC is instructed to clean these area and maintain them clean moving foreword.

findings.comment:

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the following food-contact areas in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. Base of all ice cream chest freezers (the 3 display ones) have quite a bit of fallen ice cream below the ice cream tubs. 
2. Bottom prep cooler has food debris and splash on base of the cooler.
3. Interior of the microwave in the front house has food splash. Microwave should be cleaned every 24 hours or as needed to prevent food debris build-up.
4. Shelving in the back for donut preparation is soiled on all levels of the unit. Shelving unit needs cleaned.

Discussed routine cleaning of food-contact surfaces with PIC. Ensure staff is aware to clean bottoms of cooler and freezers to remove food debris. Ensure staff is aware to clean all microwaves every 24 hours or as needed to prevent food splash build-up. Inspector will follow-up on 5/22/23.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

On arrival, the hand sink in the service area of the facility had the sani bucket for this area stored in it. PIC is instructed to ensure that all hand sinks are maintained easily accessible at all times. The bucket was moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. 

Multiple sections of the sides sections of the counters in the service areas are observed pulling away from the counter. Several of these sections are are being held on by tape. A few other sections are missing small areas. A discussion took place with both PICs during the inspection. They are aware that smooth and easily cleanable surfaces are what is required in areas involving food prep and/or moisture. They stated that replace the pieces is on the list of repairs/remodels that they have. Until then, they are instructed to remove the tape and glue/caulk/paint the areas to seal them and provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

On arrival, no CFPM was available. The CFPM are currently on vacation and will not be back into town till June 13th. A CFPM should be at the facility at all times that foods are being handled. Inspector will follow up on the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. 

An employee was observed to wash hands, then use their bare hand to turn off the faucet prior to reaching for the paper towel. A clean barrier should be used when turning off the hand sink to prevent recontamination of the hands. Education took place to correct.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). 

1) In the walk in freezer, a container of ice cream is observed left open on a shelf under the condenser. An ice stalactite is observed to be growing down next to the container and ice is observed directly next to the container. 2) A tray of donuts was observed uncovered in the walk in cooler and directly across from the fan. Foods should be covered in order to protect them from possible contamination sources. Both items were covered during the inspection to correct. 3) Boxes of donuts are observe stored on the floor in the walk in cooler. Foods should be stored at least 6 inches above the floor. The boxes were moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. 

Tape is observed holding pieces of the lid to two different display freezers together. Repair/replace the lids.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

1) Multiple locations in the back are observed with a thick accumulation of food debris on the floor. 2) The fan in the walk in cooler has an accumulation of dust and is in need of cleaning. The facility should be cleaned often enough to prevent accumulation of potential contaminants or food that could attract pests.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.

No reporting agreements are observable at the facility. The PIC is being emailed the form (as requested by them) used by SCDPH. Follow up will take place in 2 weeks.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-602.12  (C)  The panini prep in the facility is observed with a layer of char on both top and bottom surfaces. PIC is instructed to clean (wash/rinse/sanitize) often enough so as to maintain build up.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Clean utensils are observed in a soiled container on the table in the back used for food prep and in a pan on the shelf next to the 3 part sink. PIC is instructed to maintain the containers used for storing cleaned food contact surfaces clean. The containers were moved to the 3 part sink for cleaning during the inspection.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750-510d To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand sink.

Observed an employee not use a barrier to turn off the faucet at a hand sink after washing their hands. Discussed the proper procedure for hand washing with the employee and the PIC during the inspection. The employee rewashed their hands during the inspection.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

The facility is currently using a chlorine (CL) based chemical sanitizer and only has test strips intended for Quat sanitizer. Discussed with the PIC and stated that the test strips must be for the type of chemical sanitizer being used.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.
Observed multiple moist cloths stored out of solution (on counters) during the inspection. Discussed with the PIC and stated that cloths used for surfaces should be stored in their sani buckets between uses. The cloths were placed back into solution during the inspection.
